<Aside type="caution" title="Update: the serving host is the Hono host, not Next (Next retired)">
This page was written in the Next era. Since then the operator's Next.js
layer was retired (operator = Vite SPA + Hono host). The Starlight static
site is now served by the **Hono host** via `apps/operator/bin/host-docs.ts`
— it owns the bare-slug → `<slug>.html` resolution, the
`Accept: text/markdown` → `<slug>.md` twin negotiation, and the
`404.html` fallback. There is no `next.config.js` (it doesn't exist) and no
`proxy.ts`; the "Next rewrite in `afterFiles`" gotcha below is obsolete.
The MCP adapter, the `dist/` → `public/internal/docs/` postbuild copy, the
`build.format: 'file'` decision, and the URL contract are all unchanged.
</Aside>

## What changed in one paragraph

We moved every internal-docs MDX page from `apps/operator/content/internal-docs/` to `apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs/` and rebuilt the surface on Astro 6 + Starlight 0.39 + starlight-llms-txt. The MCP `docs:*` tool surface (outline / get / search) keeps the same JSON shape via a new `starlightContentAdapter` in `packages/docs-engine/`. The docs site itself ships as static HTML in `apps/operator-docs/dist/`, copied into `apps/operator/public/internal/docs/` at build time so the **Hono host** (`bin/host-docs.ts`) serves it under the existing URL contract. (A couple of stale `agent-insights/` MDX files still linger under `apps/operator/content/internal-docs/` — the move was not byte-complete, but the live source is `apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs/`.)

## The agent contract still works

- `GET /internal/docs/` — Starlight HTML home.
- `GET /internal/docs/<slug>` — HTML page (the Hono host's `host-docs.ts` resolves a bare slug to `<slug>.html`).
- `GET /internal/docs/<slug>` with `Accept: text/markdown` — clean markdown twin (`<slug>.md`).
- `GET /internal/docs/llms.txt` — index produced by starlight-llms-txt.
- `GET /internal/docs/llms-full.txt` — full corpus.
- `GET /internal/docs/llms-small.txt` — abridged corpus (new; harmless).

Per-page `Accept: text/markdown` negotiation was originally dropped at the cutover and **restored separately**. `starlight-llms-txt` only emits aggregate `llms*.txt`; we restored the per-page channel by emitting `<slug>.md` twins from `apps/operator-docs/scripts/emit-md-twins.ts` (runs after `astro build`, uses `@papercusp/docs-engine`'s `renderMdxToMarkdown` + `withPreamble`). The **Hono host** (`apps/operator/bin/host-docs.ts`) rewrites `Accept: text/markdown` on a bare slug to the static `<slug>.md` (this used to be `proxy.ts` under Next). Agents can also use the `docs:get` MCP tool (engine-side, not HTTP) or pull from `/llms-full.txt`.

## Where things live now

| Concern | Path |
|---|---|
| MDX source | `apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs/<section>/<slug>.mdx` |
| Astro config | `apps/operator-docs/astro.config.mjs` |
| Build output | `apps/operator-docs/dist/` |
| Served from | `apps/operator/public/internal/docs/` (postbuild copy), via the Hono host `apps/operator/bin/host-docs.ts` |
| MCP docs adapter | `packages/docs-engine/src/adapters/starlight.ts` |
| Engineering adapter selector | `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/docs/_engineering-adapter.ts` |
| Sidebar config | per-page frontmatter `sidebar.order` (used to be `meta.json`) |
| MCP Resources | `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/docs/resource-{index,section}.ts` |

## Gotchas to know

### 1. `build.format: 'file'` is load-bearing

Starlight default is `format: 'directory'` which emits `dist/<slug>/index.html`. We use `format: 'file'` (set in `astro.config.mjs`) which emits `dist/<slug>.html` instead. Why: serving the static files from `public/` without `format: 'file'` would need directory-index trailing-slash semantics. With `.html` files at the explicit path, the host resolves a bare slug to `<slug>.html` directly. (Originally this was a single Next rewrite; now `apps/operator/bin/host-docs.ts` does the bare-slug → `.html` resolution.)

### 2. (Obsolete) The Next rewrite is in `afterFiles`, not the top-level array

**Obsolete — Next is retired and `next.config.js` no longer exists.** This gotcha described where the docs rewrite rule lived in the Next config object (`rewrites() { return { beforeFiles, afterFiles, fallback } }`). The slug → `.html` resolution is now done in code by the Hono host (`apps/operator/bin/host-docs.ts`), not by a Next rewrite. Disregard.

### 3. Postbuild copy is in `apps/operator-docs/package.json`

The four-step chain is now `build:inner`, and `build` wraps it in a **singleflight lock**:

```jsonc
"build":       "bash scripts/docs-build-singleflight",
"build:inner": "npm run clean:preview && astro build && tsx scripts/emit-md-twins.ts && bash scripts/postbuild-copy.sh",
```

If you run `astro build` directly (or just `npx astro build`), the preview-dir cleanup, the `.md`-twin emit, and the static copy steps are all skipped and the host will serve stale content (and lose the `Accept: text/markdown` twins). **Always run `npm run build` from `apps/operator-docs/`** — never `build:inner` directly.

The wrapper exists because `astro build` writes `dist/` + `dist/.prerender` **in the shared checkout**, so two concurrent builds clobber each other (WI-1998). It coalesces: a build requested while another is running does not start a second one, because `postbuild-copy.sh` publishes atomically and the queued caller's content is already published by the in-flight run. This makes the "always run `npm run build`" rule *more* load-bearing than when this page was written — the lock only protects the path that goes through it.

### 4. Both fumadocs setups were removed

`apps/operator/source.config.ts`, `apps/operator/lib/source.ts`, `apps/operator/app/(docs)/**`, `apps/operator/app/llms.txt/`, `apps/operator/app/llms-full.txt/`, `apps/operator/app/llms.mdx/`, `apps/operator/app/api/search/` are all gone. Same paths in the old `@papercup/web` app (now retired under `_retired/papercup/`). If you find references to those, they're stale; remove or update.

### 5. The `fumadocs` plugin slug is unrelated

`@papercupai/fumadocs` (with the `@` prefix) is the name of an internal Papercusp plugin for per-harness docs viewing — NOT the npm package we removed. Plugin manifests, route handlers, and UI code may legitimately reference `fumadocs` as a slug. Don't remove those.

## Performance

⚠ **The build-time figures below are from 2026-05-20 and are stale — do not quote
them as current.** The site was 129 pages then; as of 2026-08-04 the source tree
holds **842** (829 `.mdx` + 13 `.md`), a ~6.5× growth, so the wall-clock numbers
have certainly moved. They are kept only as the migration-era baseline. (No
re-measurement was taken with this update — measure it yourself before citing one.)

A full `astro build` of the 129-page site completed in ~21s, with
Pagefind search indexing adding ~0.5s. The output is plain static HTML:
the operator serves it straight from `public/internal/docs/`, so there
is **no runtime docs cost** — no second Node process, and no per-request
MDX compilation (fumadocs compiled MDX inside the Next request path).

A head-to-head build-time / bundle-size comparison against the old
fumadocs setup isn't possible — the F10 cutover removed it before a
baseline was captured. The concrete, measurable win is the runtime one
above: docs rendering moved entirely out of the request path.
